speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show no active bacterial infection and normal blood cell counts, so I need to know if you have any history of diabetes or vascular disease, and whether the wound is red, warm, or draining fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of DVT and chronic swelling in a family member strongly suggests venous insufficiency; do you notice the wound edges are rolled, and does the area hurt more when you stand up or improve when you lie down?

REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI).
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the right lower leg wound and surrounding skin changes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The photos and your report of family history with DVT strongly suggest a venous etiology, but I need to confirm if there is significant varicose veins or skin discoloration (stasis dermatitis) around the wound before finalizing the plan.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer.
